(def seq-reduce
  (fn ([f coll]
    (if-let [s (seq coll)]
      (reduce f (first s) (next s))
      (f)))
  ([f val coll]
    ;; A chunked seq reduces a chunk at a time, as Clojure's InternalReduce
    ;; does, rather than allocating a seq per element (#446). A chunk's
    ;; elements are read by index to its count: a filter's chunk is shorter
    ;; than its array. A reduced value ends the reduction.
    (loop [val val, coll (seq coll)]
      (if coll
        (if (chunked-seq? coll)
          (let [c (chunk-first coll)
                ^long n (-count c)
                ^objects input-array (suss.bootstrap/chunk-array c)
                ^long input-offset (if (suss.bootstrap/undefined? input-array)
                                     0
                                     (suss.bootstrap/chunk-offset c))
                nval (loop [i 0 val val]
                       (if (< i n)
                         (let [nval (f val (if (suss.bootstrap/undefined? input-array)
                                              (-nth c i)
                                              (aget input-array (+ input-offset i))))]
                           (if (reduced? nval)
                             nval
                             (recur (inc i) nval)))
                         val))]
            (if (reduced? nval)
              @nval
              (recur nval (seq (chunk-rest coll)))))
          (let [nval (f val (first coll))]
            (if (reduced? nval)
              @nval
              (recur nval (next coll)))))
        val)))))
